rows.why: Item 9 asks what happens when a newly drawn code collides with one already stored, and it redraws (up to 100 tries), which matches 'a code that would repeat one already in the registry is drawn again'. No item asks about the 14-day expiry or the initial unused state, so item 9 is the closest fit.

No item asks whether a normal redemption grants access to that task alone, or whether it records who used the code and when. Item 12 shows usedBy/usedAt in list output, and item 2 is about a second code. Neither asks this question.

Item 4 asks how a typed code is normalized. The pick uppercases and strips anything outside A-Z/0-9, and the run redeemed ' cccc.cccc cccc ' against CCCC-CCCC-CCCC and got ok:true, so lowercase, spaces and dashes are all ignored.

Item 1 asks whether a code can be redeemed at the exact expiry instant. The pick treats now >= createdAt+14d as expired, and the run at exactly 14 days returned reason 'expired', so one millisecond earlier still works. Both match the scenario.

No item asks what happens when a second contributor redeems a used code, or when the original redeemer redeems the same code again. Item 2 covers redeeming a different code for a task the contributor already has, and item 3 covers which reason wins when a code is both used and expired.

Item 6 asks what revoking a used code does. The run threw 'invite code has been used', so a used code cannot be revoked, as the scenario requires. No item asks directly what redeeming an unknown or revoked code returns, so item 6 is the closest.

Item 2 asks what happens when a contributor who already has access redeems another code for the same task. The run returned reason 'already has access', and the list output shows the second code still unused.
Item 11 asks how simultaneous operations are handled. With a store that resolves after random delays, the run of concurrent redemptions gave exactly one ok:true and the rest reason 'used'.

Item 12 asks what list returns and whether it includes every state. The pick returns all of the task's codes with createdAt, expiresAt and state, plus usedBy and usedAt on used codes. In the run at day 20, after expiry, the redeemed code still showed state 'used'.
